- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts, especially after sharp declines or spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, then gradually converges toward true values — suggesting lag or delayed reaction to market signals.
- Overshoots after price spikes (e.g., 68+ → 69+), then corrects downward — implies model overreacts to short-term volatility.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to forecast lower values than true outcomes in the final 5–10 days of the horizon, especially when true values are rising.
- Strong bias toward lower values in the first 10 days of forecast, then higher values in the last 10 days — suggests model fails to capture momentum or trend continuation.
- When true values show a sharp upward trend (e.g., 60–65 → 68–70), model often underreacts or lags — correction needed for momentum capture.
- Model frequently underestimates the magnitude of price increases after a low point — especially in the 15–20 day window.
- Avoid overfitting to recent low values — model tends to “anchor” too much on recent lows, missing upward momentum.
